summary: Crotamiton 10% (cream or lotion) is a topical agent indicated for the eradication of scabies (Sarcoptes scabiei) and for the symptomatic treatment of pruritus. For scabies it is massaged into the skin of the whole body from the chin down, with a second application 24 hours later and a cleansing bath 48 hours after the last application; the course may be repeated after 7-10 days if needed. For itching it is gently massaged into affected areas and repeated as required. It should not be applied to acutely inflamed, raw or weeping skin, or near the eyes and mouth.

admin: Shake lotion well before use; for scabies apply to the whole body from the chin down, not just visible lesions
Massage thoroughly into all skin folds and creases (between fingers/toes, wrists, elbows, axillae, waist, buttocks, genital area)
Apply a second coat 24 hours after the first application
Take a cleansing bath/shower 48 hours after the last (second) application to remove the drug
Avoid contact with the eyes and mouth; do not apply to acutely inflamed, raw or weeping skin
Change clothing and bed linen the next morning and launder to reduce reinfestation
moa: Crotamiton has scabicidal activity against Sarcoptes scabiei and an antipruritic action. The precise mechanism is not fully established; it acts topically to eradicate the scabies mite and relieves itching when applied to the skin.

absolute: Known sensitivity (hypersensitivity) to crotamiton or any formulation component

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women, and it is not known whether crotamiton can cause fetal harm or affect reproduction. It should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether crotamiton is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when used in a nursing woman; avoid application to the breast/chest area to prevent infant exposure during nursing.
renal: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption from topical use is minimal.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption from topical use is minimal.

pearls: Crotamiton 10% is both scabicidal and antipruritic, useful when itch relief is also desired
Persistent itching after treatment is common (residual hypersensitivity) and is not in itself evidence of treatment failure
Treat all household and close physical contacts simultaneously to prevent reinfestation
Permethrin is generally considered first-line for scabies; crotamiton is an alternative

missed: Crotamiton is used on a defined schedule rather than as regular daily maintenance. If a scheduled scabies application (initial or 24-hour second coat) is delayed, apply it as soon as remembered and adjust the timing of the subsequent cleansing bath accordingly. For antipruritic use, simply apply when needed.
overdose: Topical overuse or excessive application increases the risk of local skin irritation rather than systemic toxicity. Discontinue use, wash off the product, and treat the skin with bland emollients. If accidentally ingested, manage with standard supportive care and contact a poison control center.
